Luria, which review and summary sources report as part of the book; the book text was not read and the sources are secondary. The link to Borges's 'Funes the Memorious' and the 'forgetting is essential to being human' idea rest on a Goodreads quote attribution and one summary, so they are hedged. Old text's sleep-sorting claims, 'brain has no unlimited storage' quote and the 'best memory people forget best' claim were not found and are dropped. A Discover piece adds that S.'s memory was not photographic and he used method-of-loci-like techniques.
facts: Moonwalking with Einstein is subtitled The Art and Science of Remembering Everything.
In 1928 a Russian journalist known as S. (Solomon Shereshevsky) came to the office of psychologist A. R. Luria claiming an unusually powerful memory.
Luria studied him for about thirty years.
S. could memorize passages in a foreign language and abstruse formulas he did not understand, and keep them for years.
S.'s mind was cluttered with trivial details and sensations; he struggled to abstract or generalize and had trouble with practical life and work.

Foer links the case to Borges's story 'Funes the Memorious', about a man cursed with perfect recall, and to the idea that forgetting is essential to being human (attribution via Goodreads and one summary).
Luria also described what he called the art of forgetting (one summary).
A Discover piece says S.'s memory was not exactly photographic and that he used techniques similar to the method of loci.

tension: A man who remembered everything could not use his mind the way other people do.
opening_idea: Open on the man who could recite a formula he did not understand years later, and what that cost him.

lessons.idea: Decide what is worth keeping before you try to remember it.
lessons.anchor: S.'s cluttered mind and trouble abstracting.
lessons.example: A project manager keeps the three decisions that matter instead of every message.

reflect_final: Which details do you keep carrying around, in notes or in your head, that you could safely let go of this week?

use_cases.situation: You are about to take notes on a long meeting.
use_cases.move: Write only the three decisions and the owner of each; S. kept everything and could not pick out what mattered.

use_cases.situation: A student at home tries to memorize a whole chapter word for word.
use_cases.move: Ask them to say the main idea first and then pick the five details worth keeping.

use_cases.situation: Your phone and notebook are full of things you never reread.
use_cases.move: Delete or archive one folder this week and notice whether you miss it.

pocket_idea: Remembering everything cost S. the ability to see patterns, so choose what to keep.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: A man who could not forget struggled to see patterns, according to Foer's retelling of Luria's case.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: In 1928 a Russian journalist came to the psychologist Luria claiming a remarkable memory. Luria studied him for thirty years: he could keep formulas he did not understand, but his mind was cluttered and he struggled to generalize. Foer uses the case to argue that forgetting is part of how a mind works.
